text:
incidents-bot: SEV2 alert - spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for private-vpc egress gateway (gateway-eu-1). Error rate 5xx >= 7% over 3m, latency p95 increased from 120ms -> 2.3s. Paging maya (on-call).
maya (on-call): acked. jumping in. any customer-facing alerts? :eyes:
eli (cust-succ): seeing a couple of customer DMs — 3 routes reporting timeouts and 502s. AcmeCorp, BrightApp, and NucleusAI first reported errors ~ 10m ago.
maya (on-call): thanks. grabbing metrics, will post chrono. anyone touching VPC peering or routing in last 30m?
simon (neteng): I rolled a peering policy change ~9m ago for a subset of private peers (to add more specific route prefixes). seeing some Rx/Tx asymmetry on gateway-eu-1 now. possible asymmetric path + SNAT state issues.
maya (on-call): OK hypothesis: egress gateway is dropping or timing out due to session table saturation after route churn. can you confirm NAT table utilization on gateway-eu-1?
mike (infra): running diagnostic cmds now. output snippet:
```
# on gw-eu-1
$ sudo conntrack -S | grep tcp
tcp      12498 flow entries

$ sudo ss -s
TCP: inuse 320, orphan 0, tw 120
```
Looks like large number of short-lived TCP sessions. ephemeral port exhaustion possible.
simon (neteng): also seeing constant flaps in BGP adjacency to peer-msa-3 around the same time as the peering policy push. when BGP flaps, existing SNAT entries get unbalanced -> retries pile up -> 502/timeouts upstream.
maya (on-call): immediate mitigation options:
- temporarily move affected customer subnets to fallback-eip-pool (dedicated egress pool) via route override
- spin up spare gateway instance and migrate traffic
- increase NAT ephemeral port allocation / table size if possible without reboot
Which is fastest?
mike (infra): fastest = route override to fallback-eip-pool (no restart). I can push a route change and announce to the mesh. doing it now as a quick blast radius-limited step for AcmeCorp/BrightApp/NucleusAI.
eng-sre-bot: deploy started: route-override/fallback-eip -> gateway-eu-2 (initiated by mike)
maya (on-call): :thumbsup: mike please post when traffic starts shifting and once metrics show improvement.
emily (cust-succ): pinging customers now that we have a mitigation in flight.
mike (infra): route change applied for the three customer prefixes at 1859876658. verifying traffic now.
simon (neteng): BGP flaps have stabilized after reverting the policy on peer-msa-3. but we still have high SNAT table usage; new flows are spiking.
maya (on-call): metrics update: at 1859876685 5xx rate down from 7% -> 2.1% and p95 latency trending down to ~350ms. still above normal but improving.
eli (cust-succ): AcmeCorp reports recovery for most calls, BrightApp sees some intermittent 502s but much better. NucleusAI reports full recovery.
maya (on-call): good. next steps: leave route override in place for 30m while we drain state on gw-eu-1 and perform deeper forensics. assign to neteng/infra to investigate root cause and harden runbook.
simon (neteng): root-cause hypothesis to investigate: peering policy change triggered short BGP flaps causing asymmetric routing. That combined with a workload spike of many short TCP connections (health check churn from a misconfigured probe) led to NAT session table saturation and ephemeral port exhaustion -> gateway returned 502s/timeouts.
mike (infra): I'll open a follow-up ticket to increase conntrack table and ephemeral port range on the gateway AMI; also add an autoscaling policy to spin up spare gateways when conntrack usage > 70% for 1m.
maya (on-call): handoff to tara (on-call-next) at 1859876800. summary for handoff: mitigation applied (route override -> gateway-eu-2), primary symptoms (5xx/timeouts) improving, affected customers (AcmeCorp, BrightApp, NucleusAI), suspected root cause (peering change + NAT table saturation), tasks: keep override for 30m, confirm no new flaps, coordinate postmortem and capacity changes.
tara (on-call-next): taking over. will keep monitoring, liaise with neteng to confirm permanent fixes. tagging simon/mike for follow-through.
eng-sre-bot: incident annotation: paging window 1859876543 -> 1859876899, mitigations applied: route-override, peer policy revert.
maya (on-call): forensics notes to capture: tcpdump from gw-eu-1 around flap window, conntrack snapshot, BGP logs from peer-msa-3, and a list of customer flows that saw retries. please attach all to the follow-up ticket.
simon (neteng): collecting logs now. sample tcpdump commands:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.11.22.33 and tcp -w /tmp/gw-eu-1-flap.pcap
sudo bgpctl show adj | grep peer-msa-3
```
I'll upload to the incident ticket.
eli (cust-succ): customer impact summary for notifications: ~3 customers, partial degraded calls for ~8 minutes, full outages for ~3 minutes for some routes. recommend targeted customer emails with timeline + apology.
maya (on-call): agree. eli please send a short timeline update and that we've put a temporary reroute in place; we'll follow up with root cause + remediation plan within 48 hours.
mike (infra): metrics now look stable: 5xx ~0.6%, p95 110ms on fallback pool. scheduling conntrack/table changes and autoscale tweaks in ticket INFRA-4523.
tara (on-call-next): taking final notes. I'll keep the route override until 1859878300 (roughly 25m) and then plan a controlled failback after verifying conntrack headroom and no BGP flaps.
eng-sre-bot: incident status -> mitigated. handoff complete. follow-up owners: simon (neteng), mike (infra), eli (cust-succ). postmortem owner munging: simon. Estimated RCA doc ETA: 48h.
maya (on-call): resolved for now. will leave a brief runbook update to add "on peering change, monitor conntrack and have route-override ready". thanks team :heart:
